item.title: PlayStation Plus Monthly Games for December: Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3+4, Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2, Amnesia: The Bunker
item.dc:creator: Adam Michel
item.description: Shred rails, fight icons and flee horrors beyond your understanding with the PlayStation Plus Monthly Games for December. Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3+4, Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2, and Amnesia: The Bunker will be available to all PlayStation Plus members* from Tuesday, December 1 to Monday January 4. Let’s take a closer look at each of […]
item.content:encoded:
Shred rails, fight icons and flee horrors beyond your understanding with the PlayStation Plus Monthly Games for December. Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3+4, Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2, and Amnesia: The Bunker will be available to all PlayStation Plus members* from Tuesday, December 1 to Monday January 4. 

Let’s take a closer look at each of the games.

Download the image

Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3+4 – Cross-Gen Edition | PS5, PS4 

Alert the neighborhood watch and grab your skate buddies because the shred’s not dead: the legendary franchise returns with Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3 + 4. Everything you loved is back, revamped with more skaters, new parks, gnarlier tricks, eardrum-shattering music and much more. Drop-in to new parks or tear it up across timeless locations from both Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3 and Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 4, authentically remade in jaw-dropping 4K** resolution with streamlined goals and the epic 2-minute format. Define your own experience in the expanded Create-A-Skater and Create-A-Park modes, including the ability to create custom goals to share with friends for the first time.

Download the image

Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 | PS5, PS4 

Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 is the ultimate Dragon Ball gaming experience, packed with thrilling action, epic battles, and endless customization options. Create your own character, explore Conton City and team up with iconic characters from the series as a teacher to train and be ready to battle against formidable enemies to rescue the flow of History. Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 also features online multiplayer modes, where you can battle against other players from around the world in epic showdowns or participate in Raid Battles to face gigantic foes with other players.

Download the image

Amnesia: The Bunker | PS4 

Amnesia: The Bunker is a first-person horror game from the makers of Soma and Amnesia. Left all alone in a desolate WW1 bunker with only one bullet remaining in the barrel, it’s up to you to face the oppressing terrors in the dark. Immerse yourself in the multiple ways of tackling survival. In the shoes of the French soldier Henri Clément, you are armed with a revolver gun, a noisy dynamo flashlight, and other scarce supplies to scavenge and craft along the way. With randomization and unpredictable behavior, no play-through is the same. Hunted by an ever-present threat reacting to your every move and sound, you must adapt your play-style to face hell. Every decision will change the outcome of how the game responds. Actions bear consequences.

Download the image

Last chance to add the PlayStation Plus Monthly Games for November

PlayStation Plus members have until Monday November 30 to add the PlayStation Plus Monthly Games for November – Dead Island 2, Tomb Raider IV – VI Remastered, Monster Train 2 – to their library.

*PlayStation Plus lineup may differ by region. Please check the PlayStation.com for details. 

**The PS5 version of the game will run native 4K at 60FPS in Fidelity Mode. 4K output requires a 4K compatible device or display.

item.title: Thank you for making Grand Theft Auto VI the biggest launch in PlayStation history
item.dc:creator: Tim Turi (he/him)
item.description: After a long wait, players finally have had the chance to jump into Grand Theft Auto VI. It’s been amazing to see the PlayStation community around the world begin their adventures in the state of Leonida. Whether you’ve been counting down the days to return to the streets of Vice City or you’re experiencing the […]
item.content:encoded:
After a long wait, players finally have had the chance to jump into Grand Theft Auto VI. It’s been amazing to see the PlayStation community around the world begin their adventures in the state of Leonida.

Whether you’ve been counting down the days to return to the streets of Vice City or you’re experiencing the Grand Theft Auto series for the very first time, we want to take a moment to say: thank you. The excitement and passion of the community have made this a truly special moment for all of us. 

Celebrating a historic launch 

The launch of GTAVI marks an extraordinary moment for gaming and entertainment, becoming the biggest game launch in PlayStation history, across three decades and five console generations. More than 39 million unique players have experienced Jason and Lucia’s story in Grand Theft Auto VI on PlayStation 5.

The PlayStation community came together in a big way to experience Grand Theft Auto VI during its launch and opening weekend. Here are a few highlights from the launch window ending November 22, 2026*:

  • GTAVI set a new record for the highest number of concurrent players for any game on PlayStation, surpassing previous records across multiplayer, free-to-play, and single-player titles.
  • Across PS5, players cumulatively logged an incredible 683 million hours of gameplay in GTAVI, reflecting the enthusiasm of the PlayStation community. Each player has spent an average of 17.4 hours exploring the state of Leonida during the game’s opening days.
  • The PlayStation community has grown, as we saw the largest number of newly connected PS5 consoles on a single day since the console’s launch, outside of end-of-year holidays. Since its launch, GTAVI was the first game played on 70% of new PS5 consoles.

These are just a few ways we’ve seen our PlayStation community come together around this incredible moment in gaming, and we’re excited to see how you continue to build and share new memories and experiences in the months ahead. 

Thank you for being part of this moment

Finally, we want to congratulate our partners at Rockstar Games for bringing this extraordinary game to players around the world and continuing a partnership with PlayStation that stretches back to Grand Theft Auto III on PlayStation 2. With GTAVI, we worked to bring the best experience on PS5 and gave players a memorable way to commemorate the game with two special limited-edition DualSense wireless controllers inspired by Vice City. We also celebrated the launch with live events including Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival in Miami this past weekend.

And to our PlayStation community, thank you for your continued passion and support, and for choosing to experience GTAVI on PS5. It’s your enthusiasm that make moments like these so meaningful for all of us.

We can’t wait to see where your adventures in Leonida take you next!

 *All figures are based on SIE internal data collected from November 19, 2026, to November 22, 2026

item.title: Grand Theft Auto VI launches tomorrow, November 19
item.dc:creator: R*Q
item.description: Jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them. But when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida — forced to rely on each other more than ever […]
item.content:encoded:
Jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them. But when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida — forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive.

Grand Theft Auto VI arrives on PlayStation 5 Thursday, November 19, available at PlayStation Store.

When the sun fades and the neon glows, everyone has something to gain — and more to lose

The game is set in the state of Leonida, home to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City and beyond in the biggest, most immersive evolution of the series yet.

Jason Duval

Jason grew up around grifters and crooks. After a stint in the Army trying to shake off his troubled teens, he found himself in the Keys doing what he knows best, working for local drug runners. Meeting Lucia could be the best or worst thing to ever happen to him. Jason knows how he’d like it to turn out but right now, it’s hard to tell.

Lucia Caminos

Lucia’s father taught her to fight as soon as she could walk, and life has been coming at her swinging ever since. Fighting for her family landed her in the Leonida Penitentiary. Sheer luck got her out but now more than anything, Lucia wants the good life her mom has dreamed of since their days in Liberty City. Instead of half-baked fantasies, Lucia is prepared to take matters into her own hands.

The sprawling state of Leonida

Leonida is made up of six regions: Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, and Mount Kalaga. Here’s a closer look at what makes each region unique.

Vice City

The glamour, hustle, and greed of America captured in a single city. Each neighborhood has something to offer, from the pastel art deco hotels and bright white sands of Ocean Beach, to the bustling panaderías of Little Cuba and the bootleg brands of the Tisha-Wocka flea market, out to the VC Port, the cruise ship capital of the world. We’re a long way from the ’80s, but Vice City is still the sun and fun capital of America

Leonida Keys

Life in this tropical archipelago isn’t flashy but it’s easy. Get your buzz on and pull up a deck chair but look out — you are right on the doorstep of some of the most beautiful and dangerous waters in all of America.

Grassrivers

You never know what lies beneath the surface of this primordial expanse. The gators may be the most famous attraction, but there are far deadlier predators and weirder discoveries among the mangroves.

Port Gellhorn

Cheap motels, shut-down attractions, and empty strip malls won’t bring the tourists back, but there’s a new economy in this once-popular vacation spot. It’s fueled by malt liquor, painkillers, and truck stop energy drinks.

Ambrosia

In the heart of Leonida, American industry and old school values still reign supreme — whatever the cost. The Allied Crystal sugar refinery provides the jobs, while the local biker gang provides almost everything else.

Mount Kalaga

A national landmark up against the state’s northern border, Mount Kalaga offers prime hunting, fishing, and off-road trails. In the lush surrounding backwoods, hillbilly mystics and paranoid radicals live far from the prying eyes of the government.

Broadcasting live across Leonida

Spanning stations including Classic Rock, Modern Hip-Hop, Pop, Metal, Dance, Latin, ‘80s, Electronic, Blues, Ballads, Talk Radio, and much more, Grand Theft Auto VI features the biggest and widest-ranging selection of in-game radio yet.

Plus, for the first time ever, Grand Theft Auto VI introduces a series of on-demand podcasts for Jason and Lucia to experience beyond Leonida’s terrestrial radio, with both radio and podcasts available to listen to in vehicles and on foot through newly introduced headphones and earbuds connected to their smartphones.

Grand Theft Auto VI

Available November 19

 PlayStation Store

item.title: Introducing Hounded: Crafting the dog adventure coming to PS5 in 2027
item.dc:creator: Julia Galus
item.description: Hey PlayStation community! We’ve been keeping a secret under wraps at Imprnt Studios and Silver Lining Interactive, and we can finally let the dog out of the bag: Hounded is heading to PS5 in 2027. Get ready to step into the paws of a brave (and incredibly adorable) Border Collie, Duke, as you help him […]
item.content:encoded:
Hey PlayStation community! We’ve been keeping a secret under wraps at Imprnt Studios and Silver Lining Interactive, and we can finally let the dog out of the bag: Hounded is heading to PS5 in 2027. Get ready to step into the paws of a brave (and incredibly adorable) Border Collie, Duke, as you help him search for his lost master in an epic journey across the conflict-torn world of Anglodia.

Hounded has been in development for just over two years, and in that time we’ve been hard at work developing our very own Motion Matching system for our main character. Along with this exciting announcement, we wanted to show you what making our passion project actually looks like behind the scenes. So, we put together our very first dev diary with a full look into how the sausage (or kibble?) gets made.

Have you ever wondered how you make a dog communicate through animation? Or what a realistic quadruped animation made from scratch looks like before it lands on your screen? We’re tackling all of that and more, while introducing the little guy who started this entire journey: Duke. Check it out.

A dog story – who is Duke?

Duke is a young, clumsy, yet loyal Border Collie. He lives in the world of Anglodia – a flintlock fantasy inspired Britain in the late 18th century. It is a beautiful and mythical land filled with mysterious technology that is coming apart at the seams under tyrannical rule. However, Duke’s interests lie outside of politics and the brewing rebellion against the crown… His master, Artemys Fletcher – a secretive key player in the resistance, has vanished. Duke’s home has been torn apart by the regime and the only thing that matters now is finding his master. 

Building a border collie from the paws up

Here’s the thing about four-legged protagonists: you can’t just reskin a two-legged skeleton and call it a day. In our earliest test builds, Duke moved like a clunky wooden table with paws. It felt terrible—Border Collies have this iconic, low-slung energy that looks like they are about to run at all times. To bring this into reality in Unreal Engine, we decided to animate all of Duke’s movement by hand, using a handcrafted Motion Matching system. Eventually, we were able to set it up so that it pulls from a library of animations based on real-world references, selects the most appropriate animation for the movement, and smooths out the whole process (for the dev team and for the players).

What does the dog say?

Giving Duke a good expressive range has easily been one of the biggest creative mountains our narrative and animation teams had to climb. While humans rely on words, smirks, and raised eyebrows, Duke has muzzle twitches, ear pivots, and whiskers. We spent a while studying canine expressions and famous animated dogs (shout out to Dug) to make sure Duke could hold his own in cinematic story moments. Every movement, every sad face, and every happy snout you will see in the game is handcrafted by our incredible animation team.

More than just a good boy – Magic of The Tide

As adorable as he looks, Duke is far from an ordinary dog. Beneath the soil of Anglodia hums an ancient, strange magic known as The Tide, and Duke is one of its wielders. He possesses unlockable abilities that no other hound has, such as the Power Bark (smash through obstacles in your way) and Power Howl (electrically charge the mysterious technology you find in the world). He can even pierce the veil to perceive ghostly echoes trapped in time, known as Imprints, reliving moments that unfolded hours before he arrived. What will he discover, and will it help him find Fletcher? 

Wishlist on PS5 today

Seeing our game come to life on PlayStation 5 is a dream come true for the whole team—you can add it to your wishlist on your console today. We’ve still got miles to run before 2027, but we wanted to put Duke on your radar early. Take the dev diary for a walk, tell us what you think of Duke, and give your own pets a solid scratch behind the ears from everyone on the crew today.

item.title: First details on MLB The Show 27
item.dc:creator: Ramone Russell
item.description: Before we dive into new information on MLB The Show 27, let’s take a look back. As we reflect on 2026, two things stand out above everything else: the incredible passion and support of the MLB The Show community, and our need to better communicate and react to community feedback going forward. Whether you’ve been […]
item.content:encoded:
Before we dive into new information on MLB The Show 27, let’s take a look back.

As we reflect on 2026, two things stand out above everything else: the incredible passion and support of the MLB The Show community, and our need to better communicate and react to community feedback going forward. Whether you’ve been playing for decades or joined us for the first time this year, you’ve helped make this another special chapter in our franchise’s history.

Community stats from MLB The Show 26

While we’re proud of what our team accomplished this year, we recognize that the heart of MLB The Show has always been its community. Since launch, you’ve hit an astonishing:

  • 1,058,402,460 home runs
  • 55,168,197 triples
  • 1,639,448,296 singles

You’ve also drawn 123,300,616 walks and racked up a staggering 2,130,551,161 strikeouts. It seems we have some work to do on our collective plate discipline and pitch recognition!

But it’s not all strikeouts. You’ve also recorded 18,666,758 Perfect-Perfect hits and scored an incredible 2,506,757,548 runs.

And if those numbers weren’t impressive enough, the community collectively spent the equivalent of 31,541 years playing MLB The Show this year.

This year was not without some issues and hopefully over the next few months we’ll show you how we’ve made improvements in a host of areas.Your stories, feedback, creativity, and passion remind us why we do what we do. We don’t take your time, trust, or support for granted, and we’re incredibly fortunate to have a community that cares so deeply about the game.

From all of us at San Diego Studio, thank you for another unforgettable year. We’re excited about what lies ahead and look forward to continuing this journey together.

Get ready for MLB The Show 27

So, what lies ahead? We’re eager to share the exciting new features and improvements coming to MLB The Show 27, but it’s still a little too early to reveal what’s in store. However, there’s one announcement we can’t wait to make: The Tech Test is officially returning for MLB The Show 27. 

Tech Tests are invaluable to the development process. They help our team identify bugs, evaluate performance, and gather meaningful feedback from the community before the game officially launches.

Now, you might be wondering: If Tech Tests are so important, why haven’t we held one since MLB The Show 23? That’s a fair question.

Game development is challenging, and each year brings its own set of difficult decisions and competing priorities. Some of those decisions resulted in us not holding Tech Tests for the past few years. We appreciate your patience, passion, and continued support, and we’re looking forward to having you be part of the process again. We will provide more details on the Tech Test in the new year. 

Now & Later Packs return, so keep playing MLB The Show 26

There is still more ahead for MLB The Show 26, and the time you spend playing can give you a head start in MLB The Show 27. Now & Later packs are coming back.

Now & Later Packs contain items you can use now in MLB The Show 26, with the added bonus of allowing you to redeem The Show Packs “later” in MLB The Show 27 at no additional cost.

Each Now & Later Pack you earn playing Diamond Dynasty Content in MLB The Show 26 on console will give out a Now & Later voucher that will automatically be redeemed into The Show Packs when logging into MLB The Show 27 on console during its standard release. Make sure you log into ‘27 with the same account you used to earn Now & Later Packs in ‘26.

While that’s all for today, in the meantime, get a head start and start earning those Now & Later Packs in MLB The Show 26.

We look forward to sharing more soon and are excited about what’s to come in 2027. In the meantime, for the latest MLB The Show news, head to TheShow.com, sign up for The Scouting Report, and follow our official social channels.

item.title: QSSR arrives in Marvel’s Spider-Man 2, Control Resonant, The Finals, Arc Raiders, No Man’s Sky, and Hell Let Loose: Vietnam
item.dc:creator: Daniel Craig
item.description: Six years after launch, PlayStation 5 is still getting better. Last month, we introduced Quick Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR), bringing AI-guided upscaling to the console you already own. Since then, there’s been a lot of interest from developers eager to try it out. We’re happy to announce that the next set of games is on […]
item.content:encoded:
Six years after launch, PlayStation 5 is still getting better. Last month, we introduced Quick Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR), bringing AI-guided upscaling to the console you already own. Since then, there’s been a lot of interest from developers eager to try it out. We’re happy to announce that the next set of games is on the way, with updates rolling out over the coming weeks. 

Built on the same foundation as PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) on PS5 Pro, QSSR can deliver sharper details, cleaner edges, and more stable images than traditional upscalers. And because it shares its interface with PSSR, it’s a natural fit for games that already support PSSR. 

Here’s what the developers have to say about it. 

Download the image

Marvel’s Spider-Man 2 featuring QSSR upscaling 

Insomniac Games 

“Having seen great results integrating QSSR in Marvel’s Wolverine, our team decided to bring it to Marvel’s Spider-Man 2 as well, in an update that’s live now! We’re excited for players to swing back into our 2023 title and see QSSR’s exciting image stability and sharpness benefits in both Fidelity and Performance modes.” 

-  Mike Fitzgerald, Head of Technology, Insomniac Games 

Control Resonant featuring QSSR upscaling 

Remedy Entertainment 

Remedy Entertainment is bringing QSSR to Control Resonant on PS5, with noticeable improvements in image stability and fine detail. 

“It’s great to see PlayStation bringing the same kind of leap on the PS5 that PSSR brought to PS5 Pro. QSSR gives Control Resonant a much more stable and detailed image, and we’ve worked closely with Sony to have it ready in an update coming in December.” 

– Erik Jansson, Senior Graphics Programmer, Remedy Entertainment 

The Finals and Arc Raiders featuring QSSR upscaling 

Embark Studios 

“With the new QSSR coming soon to Arc Raiders and The Finals, we can deliver increased sharpness, better environmental clarity and overall visual improvements to even more PlayStation players. We are very happy to see Sony’s continued investment in PlayStation technology translate into meaningful improvements for all players, bringing more immersive experiences across the PlayStation ecosystem.” 

– Mikael Linderholm, Technical Art Director, Embark Studios 

No Man’s Sky featuring QSSR upscaling 

Hello Games 

“No Man’s Sky gives players an infinite procedural universe to explore. When every star in the night sky is a real solar system players can visit, we care a great deal about the quality of every pixel. 

The team has always been passionate about pushing the boundaries of technology on PlayStation. QSSR (Quick Spectral Super Resolution) allows us to render the universe in sharper, cleaner and more beautiful detail, while delivering the best possible framerate. Look for it in the next few weeks. 

It’s another step towards making the universe of No Man’s Sky even more immersive to explore.” 

– Sean Murray, Founder, Hello Games 

Hell Let Loose: Vietnam featuring QSSR upscaling 

Expression Games 

“We’re delighted to confirm that we are adding QSSR to Hell Let Loose: Vietnam on PlayStation 5 through an upcoming update. Console visuals are something our community has been passionate about, and QSSR will bring sharper, cleaner image quality to the battlefield, from dense jungle to the chaos of a full-scale firefight. We can’t wait for our PlayStation players to see the difference.” 

– Paul Rustchynsky, Game Director, Expression Games 

Looking ahead

Like the upgraded PSSR on PS5 Pro, QSSR grew out of Project Amethyst, our ongoing collaboration with AMD. It’s another example of how that shared work continues to benefit players across platforms. 

Developers are just getting started, and we’re excited to keep working with them to bring QSSR to more games on PS5 in the coming months.

item.title: Guild Saga: Vanished Worlds brings tactical adventure to PS5 in May 2027
item.dc:creator: Yasser Saleem
item.description: We’re excited to announce that Guild Saga: Vanished Worlds is coming to PS5 in May 2027. In this story-driven tactical RPG, your first mission for the Heroes Guild takes an unexpected turn when a mysterious maelstrom leaves you stranded on an unfamiliar island. Beyond its shores lie dangerous creatures, suspicious alchemists, and a bustling town […]
item.content:encoded:
We’re excited to announce that Guild Saga: Vanished Worlds is coming to PS5 in May 2027.

In this story-driven tactical RPG, your first mission for the Heroes Guild takes an unexpected turn when a mysterious maelstrom leaves you stranded on an unfamiliar island. Beyond its shores lie dangerous creatures, suspicious alchemists, and a bustling town packed with people to meet, side quests to discover, and mysteries to unravel. 

Today, we’re sharing a new trailer and a closer look at how we’ve approached combat, companions, and exploration.

Create a hero and build your party

Create your hero’s appearance and choose their background, talents, and skills.

We wanted character building to leave room for creativity and experimentation. The progression system lets you combine skills across disciplines freely, as opposed to a more rigid class system. Skills let you deal damage, heal allies, change the environment, reposition across the battlefield, summon creatures, and alter the turn sequence. With hundreds of items, you can shape both your character’s build and their appearance, choosing gear that suits your playstyle and the look you want.

Your companions offer more opportunities to shape the party. Each brings a distinct history and personal quests, while their equipment, abilities, and attributes can be completely customized. 

Through dialogue and shared experiences, you’ll discover more about the companions you choose to bring along. Friendships and romance can become part of your journey, giving you connections to your party members beyond the battlefield.

Make each turn count

Guild Saga: Vanished Worlds features tactical turn-based combat with approximately 200 skills across ten disciplines. Express your tactical creativity by exploring how skills across different schools work together and with the environment around you.

Surface interactions and weather are an important consideration in combat. Players will need to be mindful of how surfaces interact, how weather affects the battle, and how those conditions might alter their skills.

For example, a party member with points invested in Geomancer may summon a mandrake to join the fight. A companion with Hydromancer skills can then make it rain, watering the mandrake and causing it to grow into a more formidable force. A party member with Aeromancer skills may then use lightning to electrify the puddles, paralyzing anyone standing in them. Across three disciplines, you’ve summoned an ally, strengthened it through the weather, and turned the resulting surfaces into a tactical advantage. We want players to discover combinations like this and experiment with how their party’s abilities work together.

Preparation matters too. Looting, mining, and gathering herbs provide materials you can craft into weapons, equipment, arrows, potions, and food. Whether you’re replenishing supplies or crafting new gear for a companion, taking time to explore and gather resources can help your party prepare for the next battle.

Follow your curiosity

When designing exploration, we wanted players to feel that taking their time could lead to something worth finding. The main quest gives your journey direction, but the islands also invite you to wander, speak to NPCs, and investigate what catches your attention.

You might find yourself solving a murder mystery, hunting feared monsters for bounty money, or settling a deadly dispute between farm animals. Elsewhere, you can follow the imagination of a famed explorer or uncover an alchemical conspiracy. These side quests give you reasons to get to know the archipelago’s inhabitants and become involved in their troubles, whether sinister, strange, or absurd.

We wanted that variety to make following a new lead feel exciting. A conversation that seems like a small diversion can draw you into a story with its own characters, conflicts, and discoveries. Taking a detour is an opportunity to experience another side of the world and the people inhabiting it.

Hidden treasures, puzzles, valuable crafting resources, and unexpected encounters also reward exploration. Ancient books and forgotten notes offer glimpses into the world’s past, giving curious players more to uncover along the way. 

Your adventure begins in May

We’re looking forward to welcoming PlayStation players into Guild Saga: Vanished Worlds when it launches on PS5 in May 2027. We’ll share the exact release date closer to launch.

Until then, watch the new trailer and add Guild Saga: Vanished Worlds to your wishlist on the PlayStation Store. We can’t wait for you to meet your companions, explore the Respite Archipelago, and discover the stories waiting for you.
